newsitem.title: USA: Montgomery Ward to close Lechmere, Electric Ave stores.
newsitem.headline: Montgomery Ward to close Lechmere, Electric Ave stores.

text.p: Montgomery Ward & Co. Inc. said Thursday it is seeking bankruptcy court approval to close 44 speciality stores, including its Lechmere, Home Image by Lechmere and Electric Avenue & More speciality stores.
"The decision to close these stores and the resultant job losses has been a difficult one," Montgomery Ward Chairman Roger Goddu said in a statement.

"However, we believe this is an important first step as we formulate our plan of reorganization. We are convinced that by shedding these non-core speciality formats, the company will be able to focus its energies on our full-line Montgomery Ward stores," he said.
The 125-year-old retailer filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection earlier this month after talks with lenders to restructure its debt and to obtain new financing fell apart.

About 3,200 Lechmere workers and 700 associates employed by Electric Avenue & More will be affected by the store closings, Montgomery Ward said. The company will offer new jobs at other Montgomery Ward stores to "as many associates as possible." Others would receive severance and outplacement assistance.

During a hearing Thursday in banrkuptcy court in Delaware, Montgomery Ward also received approval for $1 billion in debtor-in-possession financing, which will allow it to keep its stores running during its reorganization.
Judge Peter Walsh said he would sign an order approving the loan after General Electric Co.'s GE Capital unit withdrew a restriction on the loan at the request of the retailer's creditors.
GE Capital owns 57 percent of Montgomery Ward and all of the retailer's private-label credit card. GE agreed to extend the loan after Montgomery Ward filed for bankruptcy July 7.

GE had sought as a condition to the loan a guarantee that it could continue to operate Montgomery Ward's profitable credit card business. The retailer's private-label credit card represents 50 percent of its retail sales.

Creditors objected to the condition of the loan because they wanted time to review the credit card agreements. The creditors, which include the retailer's banks, want to be sure the 408-store chain is not being unfairly charged by GE Capital for credit card services, thus decreasing the company's value and the payout available to them in a reorganization.
A hearing has been set for Sept. 10 to determine whether the credit card agreements should be revised or be replaced with a new arrangements with more favourable terms.

Lechmere was acquired by Montgomery Ward in 1994. The speciality retailer of appliances, electronic equipment and products for the home operates 33 stores in New England, New York, Michigan, Wisconsin and Alabama, the company said.
Montgomery Ward launched the Electric Avenue & More speciality stores in 1994. There are currently 11 of the appliance, electronics and furniture stores in the Midwest, Kentucky and South Carolina.

"Our near-term strategy for store closings is to shed ancillary speciality store formats in order to gain the efficiencies inherent with focusing on only full-line Wards stores. It reduces the complexity in our business by reducing the number of strategies from four to one," Goddu said.

Montgomery Ward will concentrate on its core business and begin to implement a new merchandise strategy. The strategy emphasises providing affordable apparel, including footwear, accessories and fine jewelry, and home-related products that include furniture, appliances and home entertainment, the company said.
After the proposed store closings, the company will have 356 stores in 39 states.
